verdicts.quote: Lines 117–137 parse multipart cookies (VouchCookie_1of2, etc.) without bounds checking. Attacker sends VouchCookie_1of100000000=payload. Line 130: make([]string, 1e8) allocates 1.6 GB. Or VouchCookie_x=1 causes panic on xyArray[1]. Reachable from any internet user via /validate before authentication.
verdicts.why: R04 states the advisory's exact mechanism: the part count N is taken from the attacker-controlled cookie name suffix (VouchCookie_1ofN) in pkg/cookie/cookie.go and passed unbounded to make([]string, N), so one unauthenticated /validate request forces a huge heap allocation and OOM-kills the process. It names the same file, the same make() line (130), the same attack string shape, the same unauthenticated /validate reachability, and the same impact (OOM DoS for Vouch and every site behind it). It bundles a secondary panic (xyArray[1] on a name with no 'of'), but the allocation route is stated in its own right, so it is the advisory. Closest non-match is R37, same function neighbourhood (line 136) but a different defect: an out-of-bounds index write cookieParts[i-1] when the part index exceeds the slice length ('3of2') — an index panic, not unbounded allocation, and it explicitly treats the slice size as trusted rather than attacker-controlled. R10 (UTF-8 split boundary in splitCookie), R24 (Secure flag), R33 (gzip bomb in jwtmanager) and R57 (JWT cache size) are separate defects in other code paths.
